description: Noch allein, suche 2 bis 3 Leute. Ich baue ein Web-Spiel: Du planst eine ganze Raumfahrtmission mit festem Budget, wählst Instrumente, Satellit und Rakete, startest und siehst, ob es klappt. Mit echten NASA-Daten. Den Code baue ich mit KI. Gesucht: Design/UI, Pitch und Storytelling, Recherche zu Raumfahrt und Kosten. Teamsprache Deutsch.
summary: Orbit on a Budget is a browser game about the money side of spaceflight. You run a small space company: take a contract, pick instruments, a satellite bus and one of 12 real rockets, then launch. Prices, payloads, satellite buses and success rates come from NASA and other space agencies. Your score is research points per million dollars, and the campaign goes from a weather satellite in Earth orbit to a space station, a Moon base and Mars. Students and anyone curious learn why every kilogram and every dollar counts, and how real missions are planned.
details:
What it does

Space missions are always a trade-off between money, mass, power and risk. Most people only read about this. In Orbit on a Budget you make these choices yourself.

A NASA launch on Pegasus XL cost about $56.3M for 190 kg, a Falcon 9 about $69M for 10,670 kg. That is about 46 times cheaper per kilogram. In the game you find out such differences by playing.

How it works

  1. Take a contract at Mission control, for example a weather satellite for a national weather service.
  2. Pick instruments. Each one brings research points, but also mass, power draw and cost.
  3. Pick a satellite bus. Big buses bring their own power (NASA RSDO catalog), CubeSats need solar panels.
  4. Choose one of 12 real rockets, from Electron to Starship, and decide whether to insure the launch.
  5. Launch: the stages separate, the fairing opens and the satellite unfolds. Rockets fail as often as their real success rate says.
  6. The result shows what you spent and your research points per $1M, plus a space fact with a picture.

The money you earn pays for the next contract. Research costs money and research points: your own rocket gets cheaper with every flight, a reusable booster cuts the price again, orbital refueling opens the way to the Moon and Mars. The campaign has four levels: Earth orbit, space station, Moon base and Mars.

Benefits

  • Free, in any browser, no login, English and German.
  • A short intro guides through the first contract. Pointing at a part, rocket or the insurance explains what it does.
  • Real numbers with sources in the game. Where we had to estimate, the game says so.
  • Players see why reusable rockets matter, why satellites are built light and why some rockets are cheap per kilogram and others are not.

What we hope to achieve

More awareness for space: what missions cost, why they are worth it and how engineers decide. Teachers can use it in class, and anyone can play it at home.

Tools

HTML, CSS and JavaScript without a framework, SVG and Canvas for all graphics, Web Audio for the launch sounds, Node.js tests for the game rules, GitHub Pages for hosting.

Links

Slides (PDF, 7 slides): https://falafel08.github.io/orbit-on-a-budget/docs/Orbit-on-a-Budget_Pitch_v1.pdf

Video (28 s): https://falafel08.github.io/orbit-on-a-budget/docs/Orbit-on-a-Budget_Video_v1.mp4

Source code: https://github.com/Falafel08/orbit-on-a-budget

Use of AI

The ideas come from us. We told the AI which features we wanted and what to change, and we made every decision. Claude (Anthropic), an AI coding assistant, wrote the code from these instructions. We tested every change in the game. AI also helped us look up numbers, and we checked each one against the source linked in the game. The slide file was built with the same assistant from our content.

We use no AI-generated images, video or audio.

References

  • Background image: Cosmic Cliffs, NASA, ESA, CSA, and STScI, CC BY 4.0, https://esawebb.org/images/weic2205a/
  • Buildings, domes, rovers and rocks: Kenney Space Kit, CC0, https://kenney.nl/assets/space-kit
  • Rockets, satellites and launch scenes: drawn by our own program code
  • Launch sounds: generated in the browser with Web Audio
  • All data sources with links: in the game under Credits → Sources, and in data/SOURCES.md in the repository
  • AI coding assistant: Claude by Anthropic
  • Hosting: GitHub Pages
  • 3D engine: Three.js 0.170 with OrbitControls, MIT license, https://threejs.org/
  • Earth and Mars maps: Solar System Scope, CC BY 4.0, based on NASA imagery, https://www.solarsystemscope.com/textures/
  • Moon map: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio, CGI Moon Kit (LRO data), https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/4720
  • Space station level: food per crew member (NASA Human Research Roadmap), crew seat price (NASA OIG), Astrobee (NASA NTRS), Dextre and Canadarm2 (CSA), Robonaut 2 (IEEE Spectrum)
